module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1067

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1067](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1067)
- [BoPi24] N. Bowler and M. Pitz, A note on uncountably chromatic graphs. arXiv:2402.05984 (2024).
- [ErHa66] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems. Acta Math. Acad.
  Sci. Hungar. (1966), 61-99.
- [Ko13] Komjáth, Péter, A note on chromatic number and connectivity of infinite graphs. Israel
  J. Math. (2013), 499--506.
- [So15] Soukup, Dániel T., Trees, ladders and graphs. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (2015), 96--116.
- [Th17] Thomassen, Carsten, Infinitely connected subgraphs in graphs of uncountable chromatic
  number. Combinatorica (2017), 785--793.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Cardinal SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos1067

/--
A graph is infinitely edge-connected if to disconnect the graph requires deleting
infinitely many edges. In other words, removing any finite set of edges leaves
the graph connected.
-/
def InfinitelyEdgeConnected {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃s : Set (Sym2 V)⦄, s.Finite → (G.deleteEdges s).Connected

/--
Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain an infinitely connected subgraph with
chromatic number $\aleph_1$?

Komjáth [Ko13] proved that it is consistent that the answer is no. This was improved by
Soukup [So15], who constructed a counterexample using no extra set-theoretical assumptions. A
simpler elementary example was given by Bowler and Pitz [BoPi24].

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle and Aleph Prover.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos1067.lean"]
theorem erdos_1067 :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 →
      ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 ∧ InfinitelyConnected H.coe := by
  sorry

/--
Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain an infinitely edge-connected subgraph
with chromatic number $\aleph_1$?

Thomassen [Th17] proved that the answer is yes: every graph of uncountable chromatic number has a
subgraph with infinite edge-connectivity and uncountable chromatic number.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1067.variants.infinite_edge_connectivity :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 →
      ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 ∧ InfinitelyEdgeConnected H.coe := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Formalize variant independent of ZFC.

end Erdos1067

reformulations.difference: `InfinitelyEdgeConnected` says the graph stays `Connected` after deleting any finite `Set (Sym2 V)`. The set may contain non-edges or diagonal elements, and connectedness also forces the graph to be nonempty. Thomassen [Th17, §2] instead defines edge-connectivity as the smallest cardinality of a cut: all edges between the two sides A, B of a vertex partition. "Infinite edge-connectivity" therefore means every cut is infinite. The variant also fixes χ = ℵ₁ for both G and H, where Thomassen's Theorem 2 speaks of uncountable chromatic number.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) On a nonempty graph, `InfinitelyEdgeConnected G` holds iff every cut (A, Aᶜ) with A and Aᶜ nonempty contains infinitely many edges of G. Forward: if the cut D were finite, G minus D is still connected. A walk from A to Aᶜ then has a boundary dart (`Walk.exists_boundary_dart`), and that edge lies in D, a contradiction. Backward: suppose G minus s is disconnected. Let A be the set of vertices reachable from u. Every G-edge crossing A must lie in s, so the cut is finite, a contradiction. Deleting non-edges changes nothing. The only degenerate cases are the empty and one-vertex graphs, and these cannot be witnesses, since a witness has χ = ℵ₁ and so uncountably many vertices (also proved). (2) `H.coe.chromaticCardinal ≤ G.chromaticCardinal`. So when χ(G) = ℵ₁, a subgraph with no ℕ-colouring has `chromaticCardinal` exactly ℵ₁ (proved). Hence Thomassen's Theorem 2 gives exactly the variant's right-hand side, which is the source's ℵ₁ question.

reformulations.difference: `InfinitelyConnected` (from FormalConjecturesForMathlib) adds `Nontrivial V`. Otherwise it follows the source's definition: any two distinct vertices are joined by an infinite set of pairwise internally disjoint paths (`List.Disjoint` of interior vertex lists). The counterexample papers phrase it differently. Soukup has "no uncountable ω-connected subgraphs", and Bowler–Pitz have "every uncountable vertex set contains two points joined by only finitely many independent paths". Lean's `G.Subgraph` is also not required to be induced.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A witness H has χ = ℵ₁, so its vertex set is uncountable (proved in Lean). The `Nontrivial` clause is therefore automatic. For graphs with at least two vertices, "infinitely many internally disjoint u–v paths for all u ≠ v" is equivalent to "connected after deleting any finite vertex set". One direction: finitely many deleted vertices meet only finitely many of the paths. The other is a greedy argument: after removing the finite set of interior vertices used so far, a new u–v path still exists (with a length ≥ 2 detour when u and v are adjacent). Induced versus arbitrary subgraphs makes no difference either. Taking the induced subgraph on H.verts keeps connectivity, and its χ lies between χ(H) = ℵ₁ and χ(G) = ℵ₁. Paths in H map injectively to independent paths in G, so the Bowler–Pitz property refutes `InfinitelyConnected H.coe` for every such H.

review.notes:
No misformalization found. Both theorems state what the primary literature poses, and both answers and categories are correct.

1. The erdosproblems.com page disagrees with the cited paper, and the file is right. The page (last edited 18 Jan 2026; LaTeX-source snapshot of 9 Jul 2026) says: "Thomassen [Th17] constructed a counterexample to the version which asks for infinite edge-connectivity." Thomassen's paper says the opposite:
   - Abstract: "We prove that every graph of uncountable chromatic number has a subgraph which has uncountable chromatic number and infinite edge-connectivity."
   - Theorem 2 states the same result.
   - Introduction: "In this paper we prove that the edge-connectivity version of the conjecture is true."
   The variant's `answer(True)` and its docstring follow Th17 and are correct. The site's remark is the error. Maintainers should not "fix" the variant to match the site, and may want to tell erdosproblems.com.

2. Lean checks (scratch files in /workspace/review):
   - `InternallyDisjoint` uses `List.Disjoint` on interior vertex lists.
   - `ℵ_ 1` is definitionally `aleph 1 = ℵ₁`, and everything is in universe 0.
   - The hypothesis χ(G) = ℵ₁ is satisfiable: I proved it for the complete graph on `(ℵ_ 1).out`.
   - Any `H` with `H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1` has uncountable `H.verts`. So the degenerate one-vertex case (vacuously `InfinitelyEdgeConnected`) can never be a witness.
   - `InfinitelyEdgeConnected` matches Thomassen's cut definition on nonempty graphs.
   - `H.coe.chromaticCardinal ≤ G.chromaticCardinal`, and an uncountably chromatic subgraph of a χ = ℵ₁ graph has χ = ℵ₁.
   - Together these show Th17's Theorem 2 implies the variant's right-hand side.
   - For the main theorem: Bowler–Pitz's graph has χ = ℵ₁ exactly, and every uncountable vertex set contains two vertices joined by only finitely many independent paths. That refutes `InfinitelyConnected H.coe` for every H with χ = ℵ₁, so `answer(False)` is right. Soukup's abstract ("graphs of chromatic number ω₁ without uncountable ω-connected subgraphs") agrees.

3. The `formal_proof` link does not prove the repository statement verbatim. The plby file proves `¬erdos_1067.{1}` with its own encodings:
   - the counterexample graph lives on `T_struct : Type 1`;
   - subgraphs are induced;
   - χ = ℵ₁ is encoded as an ω₁-colouring plus no ℕ-colouring;
   - connectivity is encoded as `¬ finite_independent_paths` over walks.
   Its conclusion implies the FC statement's mathematical content. But the FC theorem quantifies over `V : Type`, so a universe transfer (showing `T_struct` is `Small.{0}`) is still needed, as PROOFS.md's "linked statement implies the repository statement" check would require. The link also points to `blob/main` rather than a pinned commit, a common pattern across the repository's 290 plby links. This is not a defect in the statement.

4. The live erdosproblems.com page could not be fetched (Cloudflare), so I relied on Wayback snapshots from 9 Jul 2026 of the problem page, its LaTeX source and the forum thread. The ℵ₁-vertex variant, which is independent of ZFC, is correctly left as a TODO.
